trust_decision.summary: The branch/base ref and reference sha that reach `git` are attacker-influenced (ARGOS_BRANCH / ARGOS_REFERENCE_BRANCH / ARGOS_REFERENCE_COMMIT, CI env vars, project default base branch), so they must be handed to git as argv elements rather than interpolated into a shell command line; the decision is made inside the internal git wrapper of @argos-ci/core.

landing_point.why: The advisory names an OS command injection via a CI branch name in @argos-ci/core; grepping the branch/ref value into a shell lands first on the only interpolated merge-base call, which is also the sink the published PoC test exercises.

fix_sites.entry_point: `argos upload` CLI (packages/cli/src/commands/upload.ts:122) and upload() from @argos-ci/core -> getMergeBaseCommitSha (packages/core/src/ci-environment/index.ts:44) -> packages/core/src/upload.ts:292
fix_sites.module_kind: internal git helper module (not exported from packages/core/src/index.ts)

fix_sites.entry_point: same getMergeBaseCommitSha loop at packages/core/src/ci-environment/git.ts:122-133 (ref + target interpolated into `git fetch`)
listParentCommits (packages/core/src/ci-environment/index.ts:59) via packages/core/src/upload.ts:310; also the debug-only listing at packages/core/src/ci-environment/git.ts:136-137
listParentCommits -> `git fetch --depth=200 origin <sha>` from packages/core/src/upload.ts:310 (referenceCommit from config or the /project API response)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue that only the user-supplied --reference-branch / ARGOS_REFERENCE_BRANCH value is untrusted, while the CI-derived branch (packages/core/src/ci-environment/services/github-actions.ts:101-115, gitlab.ts:28), the server-supplied defaultBaseBranch (packages/core/src/upload.ts:274,290) and referenceCommit are 'trusted environment values', so the merge-base path alone needs hardening.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: gitMergeBase must keep returning null (not throw) when git exits with status 1 and empty stderr, the legitimate 'no merge base found' outcome that upload.ts uses to fall back; a fix that throws on any git failure, or that stops preserving execFileSync's status/stderr error shape, breaks that path. Adjacent: the `<ref>:<target>` refspec must stay a single argv element with its colon intact.

O6_input_shapes: branch/ref containing shell metacharacters such as $(...), backticks, ';' and spaces (merge-base positionals, git.ts:67)
refspec `<ref>:<target>` where the colon must survive argument splitting (git.ts:89 -> 97-105)
numeric depth and --max-count values passed as argv strings (git.ts:99, git.ts:113-118)
an argument containing shell double quotes: pre-fix `--format="%H"` relied on the shell stripping the quotes, post-fix it is the literal `--format=%H` (git.ts:154 -> 115)
an optional argument that is absent (maxCount undefined) rather than an empty string (git.ts:113-118, pre-fix masked by .trim())
a raw sha string in the fetch positional (git.ts:162 -> 129)

O7_producer.where: packages/core/src/config.ts:445-459 (branch:448, referenceBranch:456, referenceCommit:458), assembling options / ARGOS_* env / CI env through the convict schema at packages/core/src/config.ts:119-123 and 188-199, where all three are plain `format: String` with no ref validation

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second git helper in a different package that runs git through the shell (`exec`) and could take a caller-supplied path/ref
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this file already executes git via a shell with a static command and is consumed across packages (packages/playwright/src/metadata.ts:139,185); extending it with `getGitLog(path)` or `resolveRef(ref)` that interpolates is a natural maintainer change in the same house style as the pre-fix core code

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a CI-service-local ref resolution, e.g. running `git rev-parse --verify ${branch}` or `git fetch origin ${ref}` inside the service config instead of delegating to the shared helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: each service already shapes the branch string itself (refs/heads stripping here, raw CI_COMMIT_REF_NAME at services/gitlab.ts:28); resolving that branch locally before merge-base is an unsurprising service-level addition

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a composition route that computes a second merge base for the pull-request base branch with its own shell invocation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the reference-commit selection here already blends referenceBranch, prBaseBranch and the server default; adding a fallback that asks git directly for the other candidate is a realistic wrapper-level change

O9_family: CWE-78 OS command injection: VCS refs and shas interpolated into shell command lines

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js >=22 (package.json engines: node 22, .nvmrc), pnpm 11.3.0 workspaces, turbo, tsdown for build, vitest for tests; `git` binary required at runtime
O10_build.project_tests: packages/core/src/ci-environment/git.test.ts (at the pinned commit: one `#head` assertion plus skipped `#branch`/`#getRepositoryURL`); run with vitest in packages/core (package.json script `test`)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Regex-validate or shell-quote the branch name inside gitMergeBase only (the PoC path), leaving the other three shell invocations - notably the debug `git log` listing and the reference-commit fetch - interpolated.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix's own argv conversion still passes refs/shas as bare positionals with no `--` terminator and no ref validation (e.g. packages/core/src/ci-environment/git.ts:97-105), leaving a possible argument-injection shape; not pursued, and not listed as O8 because the published fix did touch those call sites.
